newsitem.title: GERMANY: German building employers offer fresh wage talks.
newsitem.headline: German building employers offer fresh wage talks.

text.p: Employers in Germany's troubled construction sector on Tuesday offered the IG Bau building union fresh wage talks and said that negotiations could take place this week.

Wilhelm Kuechler, vice-president of the employers' representative group the HDB, said after a meeting of employers in Mainz that the talks would have to take place without pre-conditions by IG Bauen-Agrar-Umwelt (IG Bau).
The offer came after IG Bau's wages commission on Monday urged union leaders to reject an arbitration-brokered pay deal.
The employers went on to say that the mediator in the wages dispute, the Christian Democrat politician Heiner Geissler, should come up with new proposals on the issue of sick-pay.
Kuechler said that IG Bau should not make the full payment of sick pay a pre-condition for discussions.

IG Bau was demanding that its members receive 100 percent of sick pay benefits, while the pay-deal brokered by the arbitrator allowed for a payment of 80 percent of sick pay benefits for the first three weeks of illness.
Meanwhile in Bonn, Peter Huber, vice-president of ZDB building employers union, said there was no way it could accept the conditions set out by the union with no ifs or buts.
If a deal is not approved by May 21, IG Bau can lawfully call for industrial action.
